title: plugin-ui-gaps: Close the declarative model's capability gaps + make the translator self-maintaining
summary: Widgets can do things the ViewNode model cannot say. Close the gaps and remove the hand-written prop list in realize so they cannot come back.
description:
═══ WHY THIS PHASE EXISTS ═══

Split out of F003/P011/T006 (typed builder SDK) on 2026-07-25, after research the user asked for.
T006 was going to build a typed builder on top of the CURRENT prop vocabulary. That would have
frozen a set of holes into a compile-checked API — the builder would make it *impossible* to write
a padding, which is worse than today's silent ignore. This phase corrects the model first; T006
then builds the typed builders on top of a corrected model.

═══ THE CORE DEFECT ═══

`heca/src/chrome/realize.rs` hand-writes a reader for every property, per widget. When someone adds
a builder to a widget in `heca-grid-ui`, nothing forces the matching reader to be added. It has
been forgotten repeatedly. The capability exists in the widget and is unreachable from a
`ViewNode` — silently, with no warning, no log, no test failure.

Verified by listing every property-name string literal `realize.rs` actually reads and diffing it
against the widgets' real builder APIs (2026-07-25, on main @ d698916).

═══ THE FULL GAP LIST (each verified in code) ═══

REAL GAPS — the widget can do it, a ViewNode cannot say it:

1. `padding` (and `justify`, `width`, `height`, `direction`, margins, spacing tokens).
   `realize_flex` (realize.rs:440-459) reads ONLY `gap` and `align`. Everything else on `Style`
   is unreachable. NOTE: the original design doc writes `Column::new().gap(8).padding(12)` at
   pluggable-chrome-plugin-plan.md:340 — the very line introducing the builder SDK. Padding was
   intended from day one and simply never got a property. This is an oversight, not illustration.

2. `Input` placeholder. `Input::placeholder()` exists (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/input.rs:122) and
   the showcase uses it twice, including the command palette (showcase.rs:264, 698). The realize
   arm (realize.rs:163-176) reads only value + `name` + change intent.

3. `Scroll` axes. `ScrollRegion` supports both axes: `new()` (vertical), `horizontal()`, `both()`,
   `axes(ScrollAxes)` (scroll_region.rs:186-247). The showcase depends on it — its entire root is
   `ScrollRegion::new().both()` (showcase.rs:1897) plus a `.both()` grid demo (showcase.rs:1401).
   realize maps `WidgetKind::Scroll` to a bare `ScrollRegion::new()` (realize.rs:133), so anything
   declarative is vertical forever.

4. The clickable `Row` widget is unreachable, AND ITS NAME COLLIDES.
   `heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/row.rs` is a focusable, clickable container — hover tint, active
   marker with `ActiveMarker`, press flash, focus ring, `on_activate` (mouse + Enter/Space),
   described as `Item`'s open cousin for rich clickable dock rows.
   `WidgetKind::Row` does NOT map to it. It maps to `Flex::row()` — a plain horizontal box with no
   interactivity (realize.rs:124). Two different things share one name, and the interactive one has
   no declarative spelling at all. docs/plugin-authoring.md example 2 writes exactly this
   (`Row::new().gap(12)...on_press(intent(...))`) against a kind that cannot do it.

5. `Separator` has no `WidgetKind`. The widget exists (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/separator.rs —
   `horizontal()`, `vertical()`, `length()`); the vocabulary has no entry. docs/plugin-authoring.md
   example 2 uses `Separator::new()`.

6. `PropValue::Color` is DEAD. Declared in the model (view.rs:201-202, documented as "#rrggbb /
   #rrggbbaa, or a theme color token name") and read by NOTHING — grep of realize.rs finds only
   `glyph_prop`, never a colour reader. Either wire it to theme token names or remove it.

DOC ERRORS — the docs promise things that have no native equivalent either:

7. `Panel::new().title("Hello")` (plugin-authoring.md example 1, README). There is no Panel widget:
   `WidgetKind::Panel` realizes to a plain `Surface` (realize.rs:129-131, comment says so), and
   `Surface` has no title (surface.rs — only `new`/`row`/`column`). `Card` is the titled one.

8. `Label::new(..).variant(Variant::Muted)` (plugin-authoring.md example 2). `Label` has no variant
   natively (label.rs — align/color/bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/font_size/font_scale), and
   `ViewVariant` is button-shaped: Primary, Secondary, Destructive, Outline, Ghost, Link — no
   Muted (view.rs:169-176). Muted text is a COLOUR, which ties this to gap 6.

═══ THE PLUMBING DECISION (user-driven, 2026-07-25) ═══

The user rejected "just add the missing readers": adding a reader per property means the next
property is forgotten too. They also rejected a single `apply_style_props()` function, correctly
noting it STILL needs a line per new field — it moves the drift, it does not remove it.

Agreed direction: the property list must BE A TYPE that a generator reads, never a function body
someone remembers to update. That splits by layer:

LAYER A — layout settings. They do not live on the widgets. They all live on one `Style` struct
(heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs:211) hanging off `Base`, which every widget embeds. Make `Style`
(the layout part) able to read and write itself, then merge a node's properties into it. Add a
field later and it works with zero code anywhere.
  PRECEDENT ALREADY IN THE CODE: `realize` (realize.rs:100-112) already applies `align_self` and
  `justify_self` generically for every kind, with the comment "read it once here rather than in
  each arm". The right pattern was started and not finished — that is exactly why `gap` works only
  inside `realize_flex` while `align_self` works everywhere.

LAYER B — settings that belong to one widget (placeholder, axes, checked, severity, value). These
are fields on individual widget structs; nothing generic reaches them. A small code generator over
the widgets' own builder methods writes the translation.

After both, realize.rs contains NO property-name list at all and cannot fall behind.

═══ BLOCKER ON LAYER A: `Style` MIXES LAYOUT WITH VISUALS ═══

A whole-struct merge would hand plugins raw colours. `Style` holds `fill`, `border`, `glow`,
`accent`, `fg`, `radius` (style.rs:289-295) in the same struct as `padding` and `width`.
"Styling is not a property — the plugin picks intent (danger/accent/size), the host resolves the
actual pixels from the Theme" is rule C of pluggable-chrome-plugin-plan.md §2.6.1 and is repeated
in AGENTS.md's SETTLED table ("Is styling a prop? NO").
⇒ The layout/visual boundary must become a TYPE, not a reviewer's memory. See T1.

Also note: `heca-grid-ui` currently has NO serialization dependency at all — its dependencies are
heca-core, heca-theme, floem_reactive, taffy (heca-grid-ui/Cargo.toml:8-12), and `Style` derives
only `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq` (style.rs:210). Layer A adds that, plus derives down through
`Length`, `Align`, `Justify`, `Direction`, `Spacing`, `WidgetSize`, `GridCell`.

═══ SETTLED CONSTRAINTS — DO NOT RE-OPEN (AGENTS.md:730-796) ═══

- `heca (app) ──depends on──▶ heca-grid-ui (library)`. NEVER the reverse.
- `heca-grid-ui` must NOT own `ViewNode`, and `Button::new(ViewNode)` is impossible.
- `realize` is the ONE ViewNode→widget bridge, app-side.
- Behaviour crosses as an `Intent` (action id + args), never a callback.
- Styling is not a property; semantic variant/size/align + colour/glyph NAMES only.
- A widget whose state is a live host signal is HOST-ONLY (`ScrollBar`; also individual builders
  like `DockFrame::rail(..)`).
- Any code generator added for Layer B must keep `heca-grid-ui` free of `ViewNode`: the library
  may only gain a NEUTRAL scalar type, never the app's model.

═══ WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THIS PHASE — F003/P011/T006 RESUMES ═══

⇒ **The typed builder SDK is F003/P011/T006. It STAYS in F003/P011 — it was NOT moved here.**
Only the model corrections live in this phase. T006 is the consumer that motivated them.

T006 status: `planned` (set back from `in-progress` on 2026-07-25 — it was started, then this phase
was split out of it; nobody is working on it).

START T006 WHEN: T1-T8 of this phase are done. T9 is DEFERRED and is NOT a prerequisite — it is a
recorded question for the WASM phase, not work.
The three decisions T006 needs, all settled here rather than there:
  - T6 — how the interactive row is named (it determines the builder type name).
  - T7 — whether a description may name a theme colour (it determines whether a colour builder exists).
  - T2/T3 — the final property names, since each typed builder method maps to one.
T006's own shape was already researched on 2026-07-25 and needs no re-deriving: per-kind types with
shared traits, plain names behind a module (they collide with the native widget names that
realize.rs imports), all 30 kinds, guarded by a coverage test modelled on `WidgetKind::ALL`. The
spelling is fixed by three documents that already agree — pluggable-chrome-plugin-plan.md §2.6.1
(line ~252) and §2.6.2 (line ~340), docs/plugin-authoring.md examples 1-3, and README.md's Plugins
section.
NOTE on T006's description: its line "the WASM SDK re-exports it" cannot be literally true while the
model lives in the app crate. See T9.

═══ OPEN QUESTION, DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED HERE ═══

For a Rust plugin to get editor suggestions, the builder types must live somewhere a plugin can
depend on. Today the model is inside the app (`heca/src/chrome/view.rs`) and a plugin cannot depend
on the app. The workspace has six members and none is a plugin kit
(Cargo.toml:2 — heca-core, heca-renderer, heca-config, heca-grid-ui, heca, heca-theme); the plan
never names one either. This is NOT the thing AGENTS.md forbids (that rule is about pushing the
model down into heca-grid-ui) — a separate small crate alongside is a different question. But it is
the only way F003/P011/T006's sentence "the WASM SDK re-exports it" can ever be true. Recorded as
T9 (deferred), and CROSS-REFERENCED into the phase that must answer it: F003/P001 (plugin-08: WASM
plugin runtime) and its T1 (Design WASM host API facade).

═══ WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS ═══

Nothing in an editor ever showed an author what was available — a property is a piece of text, and
no editor can suggest text. That is HOW the holes stayed hidden. `.prop("padding", PropValue::Int(12))`
looks completely correct, is the obvious thing to write, has no effect, and nothing reports it.

═══ RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER WORK ═══

- F003/P011/T006 (typed builder SDK) — the follow-on. See the dedicated section above.
- F003/P011/T007 (Table widget) — deferred 2026-07-25, unrelated. No consumer; the task is
  explicitly "on demand".
- F003/P011/T008 (author docs) — the docs are already written and complete; T8 here corrects the two
  errors in them plus the stale BACKLOG.md pointer.
- F003/P001 (plugin-08: WASM plugin runtime) — carries T9's question; cross-referenced both ways.

═══ MANDATORY ON EVERY TASK (AGENTS.md:811-819) ═══

Whenever a widget OR the declarative model (ViewNode, props, Intents) is touched, BOTH must be
updated in the same change: (1) full rustdoc on the type/fields/methods — never reduce to a bare
pointer; (2) `docs/widgets.md`. The props-by-kind table in view.rs's rustdoc (view.rs:311-337) and
the matching section in docs/widgets.md are the two places that must stay in sync.

tasks.title: Separate layout settings from visual settings in Style (make the plugin boundary a type)
tasks.description:
PREREQUISITE for T2. Do this first — T2's whole-struct merge is unsafe until it lands.

CURRENT STATE
`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs:211` — one flat `Style` struct, `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]`
(style.rs:210), embedded in `Base` on every widget. It mixes two categories:
- LAYOUT (plugin-writable): direction, justify, align, align_self, justify_items, justify_self, gap,
  margin + per-side overrides, padding + padding_x/padding_y, pad_spacing_x/y, gap_spacing, width,
  height, min_width, min_height, max_width, max_height, flex_grow, flex_shrink, hidden, grid_cell.
- VISUAL (host/theme-owned, NEVER plugin-writable): fill, border, glow, accent, fg, radius,
  font_size, font_scale, size, size_explicit (style.rs:289-315).

WHY
"Styling is not a property — the plugin picks intent, the host resolves the pixels from the Theme"
is rule C of pluggable-chrome-plugin-plan.md §2.6.1 and appears in AGENTS.md's SETTLED table
("Is styling a prop? NO"). T2 merges a node's properties straight into the layout settings; if the
two categories stay in one struct, that merge hands plugins raw colours and borders. The boundary
must be enforced by the type system, not by whoever reviews the next PR.

BORDERLINE — decide explicitly and record the reasoning in the task:
- `size` / `size_explicit` / `font_scale` are SEMANTIC (Small/Normal/Big), already exposed as the
  `size` property and legitimately plugin-writable. They are visual by category but allowed by rule.
  Suggest a third group, or an allow-marker on the visual side. Do NOT silently lump them in.
- `hidden` and `grid_cell` are layout, not visual, despite sitting near the visual block.

WORK
- Group the fields. Preferred: nested `Style { layout: Layout, visual: Visual, .. }`. `Style` is
  `Copy` and flat today and is touched by every widget plus the layout pass, so a nested split is a
  wide mechanical change — measure it before committing to the shape. A flat struct with a derive
  marker per field is the fallback if nesting proves too invasive.
- Keep every existing call site compiling. `LayoutExt`/`StyleExt` (heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs)
  write through `base_mut().style` and must keep working unchanged — this is a data reorganisation,
  not an API change.
- `StyleExt` is deliberately NOT implemented for `Flex` (builders.rs:1-10) so a layout-only
  container cannot become a styled surface. Preserve that.

BEHAVIOUR TO PRESERVE
Everything visual. This task must produce ZERO rendering change. Per AGENTS.md, green tests are not
verification for anything visual — build the showcase and have the user look before closing.

ACCEPTANCE
- Layout and visual fields are separately addressable as types.
- Full workspace green, clippy clean under --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings.
- No visual diff in the showcase (user-verified).

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-07-25 — commit 8718718 on branch feat/p017-t1-style-split. User verified in the showcase: no visual change.

SHAPE SHIPPED (differs from the "preferred" one in the original description — the user chose it):
    pub struct Style { pub layout: Layout, pub visual: Visual }
Two PEERS, neither privileged. Not `Style { ...layout fields flat..., visual: Visual }`, which was
built first and then redone: that version needed `#[serde(skip)]` on the visual field for T2, i.e.
ONE line whose deletion would silently make colours plugin-writable. The peer shape needs no serde
attribute at all — `Layout` will derive serialization in T2, `Visual` simply will not. style.rs now
contains ZERO serde attributes. That is the whole point: nothing to forget, and the default outcome
is correct on both sides.

FIELD ASSIGNMENT + REASONING
- `Layout` (caller-owned, will be serializable): direction, justify, align, align_self,
  justify_items, justify_self, gap, gap_spacing, margin + 4 per-side overrides, padding,
  padding_x/y, pad_spacing_x/y, width, height, min/max width+height, flex_grow, flex_shrink,
  hidden, grid_cell, size, size_explicit.
- `Visual` (theme-owned, never serializable): fill, border, glow, radius, font_size, font_scale.
- `size`/`size_explicit` → Layout: SEMANTIC (Small/Normal/Big), not a pixel value, and the layout
  pass reads it and cascades it to children. `set_size` moved to Layout.
- `font_scale` → Visual: a RAW multiplier. The semantic route a description may take is `size`.
- `to_taffy()` / `to_taffy_grid()` moved onto `Layout` — they read only those fields.

DEAD CODE REMOVED: `Style::accent` and `Style::fg`. Declared with hardcoded colour literals in the
Default impl (Color::rgb(137,180,250) / (205,214,244)) and never read or written anywhere in the
workspace — widgets go through `theme.colors.accent`. Compiler-confirmed unused.

MEASUREMENT (for T2 and anyone sizing similar work): 52 files, ~200 layout accesses, ~25 visual.
A grep for `.style.<field>` UNDERCOUNTS badly — many sites reach fields through a `&Style` binding
(`let s = &mut base.style; s.padding_x = ..`). Those were fixed by rebinding to `.style.layout`,
which left the block bodies untouched. Use `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` to enumerate:
plain `--workspace` skips examples and tests, and heca-renderer/examples/showcase.rs plus
heca-grid-ui/tests/phase_a.rs both needed the rewrite.

NEW EXPORTS: `Layout` and `Visual` alongside `Style` from the heca-grid-ui crate root (lib.rs:64).

VERIFICATION: 899 tests pass, 0 failures. clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings
exits 0 (only the pre-existing `block v0.1.6` future-incompat note). Builder API unchanged —
`.gap()`, `.fill()`, `.font_size()` behave exactly as before; LayoutExt/StyleExt write to the
correct half internally, and StyleExt is still NOT implemented for Flex.

DOCS: docs/widgets.md §`Style` & layout enums rewritten for the pair, including why `size` is on
one side and `font_scale` the other, and stating that builder calls did not change.

checklist.title: Inventory every Style field into layout / visual / semantic-allowed, with the reasoning written down
Decide the shape (nested structs vs per-field markers) after measuring the call-site blast radius
Apply the split; keep LayoutExt/StyleExt call sites unchanged
Preserve StyleExt NOT being implemented for Flex
Workspace green + clippy clean
USER verifies zero visual change in the showcase

tasks.title: Layout settings: self-describing, applied to every widget kind, zero per-property code
tasks.description:
DEPENDS ON T1 (the layout/visual split). Closes gap 1 of the phase description.

CURRENT STATE
`realize_flex` (heca/src/chrome/realize.rs:440-459) reads exactly TWO layout properties — `gap` and
`align` — and only for `Column`/`Row`. Every other layout setting on `Style` is unreachable from a
`ViewNode`: padding, justify, width, height, direction, margins, min/max sizes, flex_grow,
flex_shrink, the spacing tokens, hidden, grid_cell.

THE PRECEDENT TO FINISH (not invent)
`realize` already applies two properties generically for EVERY kind, at realize.rs:100-112:
    let mut realized = realize_kind(node, emit, hints, forms);
    if let Some(align) = align_prop(node, "align_self") { ...base_mut().style.align_self = ... }
    if let Some(justify) = align_prop(node, "justify_self") { ... }
with the comment: "Self-alignment is a property of the node *inside its parent*, so it applies to
every kind — read it once here rather than in each arm."
That is the correct pattern, started and abandoned. This task finishes it.

WHY NOT A HAND-WRITTEN apply_style_props()
Explicitly rejected by the user 2026-07-25: a function listing each field still needs a new line
every time a `Style` field is added. It relocates the drift instead of removing it. The property
list must BE A TYPE that a generator reads.

WORK
- Add serialization to the LAYOUT group produced by T1. `heca-grid-ui` has NO serialization
  dependency today (Cargo.toml:8-12 — heca-core, heca-theme, floem_reactive, taffy), so this adds
  one, plus derives on the types the layout group holds: `Length`, `Align`, `Justify`, `Direction`,
  `Spacing`, `GridCell` (and `WidgetSize` if T1 puts the semantic group here).
- In `realize`, merge the node's properties into the realized widget's layout settings, replacing
  the two hand-written blocks at realize.rs:104-111 AND the gap/align reads in realize_flex.
- Property NAMES must match the field names so the mapping needs no table. Where a field name is a
  poor public name, rename the field rather than adding a lookup — a lookup is the drift again.

EDGE CASES
- Untrusted input: `realize` is TOTAL by design (view.rs rustdoc: "Missing/mistyped props are
  ignored (the widget keeps its default)"). A bad value must leave the default in place, never
  panic and never abort the rest of the merge. Keep this behaviour and test it.
- Widgets set deliberate non-default layout in their constructors — e.g. `ScrollRegion::new()` sets
  min_width/min_height to Px(0.0), flex_shrink Some(1.0), pad_spacing_y and gap_spacing
  (scroll_region.rs:188-214), each with a comment explaining why. The merge must apply ON TOP of
  the constructed widget, overriding only properties the node actually carries. Never build from a
  default `Style`, or every ScrollRegion silently stops scrolling.
- `size` is already read via `size_prop` (realize.rs:493, 946) and cascades to children. Do not
  double-apply it.

ACCEPTANCE
- Every layout setting is reachable from a `ViewNode` on every kind.
- realize.rs contains NO list of layout property names.
- A test proves a new `Style` field is reachable with no change to realize.rs.
- Totality test: nonsense values are ignored, defaults survive, nothing panics.
- ScrollRegion's constructor-set layout survives a merge that does not mention those fields.
- Update BOTH the props-by-kind table in view.rs's rustdoc (view.rs:311-337) and docs/widgets.md.

checklist.title: Add serialization to the layout group from T1 + the types it holds
Replace the align_self/justify_self blocks and realize_flex's gap/align reads with one generic merge
Align property names to field names; rename fields rather than adding a lookup table
Merge ON TOP of the constructed widget — verify ScrollRegion's constructor defaults survive
Totality test: mistyped/unknown values ignored, no panic
Test that a newly added Style field works with no realize.rs change
Update view.rs props table + docs/widgets.md

tasks.title: Generated translation for widget-specific settings + a drift test that fails on a missing one
tasks.description:
Layer B of the plumbing decision. Independent of T1/T2 (which handle layout) but shares their goal:
realize.rs must stop containing a hand-written list of property names.

CURRENT STATE
Settings that belong to ONE widget — placeholder, scroll axes, checked, on, severity, value,
selected, expanded, active, frameless, nav_selected, dismissible, action_text, body — are fields on
individual widget structs. Nothing generic reaches them, so `realize_kind`
(heca/src/chrome/realize.rs:114+) hand-writes an arm per kind, each naming its properties as string
literals. When a builder is added to a widget, nothing forces the arm to be updated. That is how
gaps 2 and 3 (placeholder, scroll axes) happened.

WORK
- Add a uniform setter to `heca-grid-ui`: a trait along the lines of
  `fn set_prop(&mut self, key: &str, value: PropInput) -> bool`, plus a small code generator that
  writes the implementation from the widget's own annotated builder methods.
- `realize_kind` then shrinks to: construct the widget for the kind, then feed it the node's
  properties. No property names in the app.

HARD CONSTRAINT (AGENTS.md:739-746, SETTLED)
`heca-grid-ui` must NEVER see `ViewNode`, `PropValue`, or anything else from the app — the app
depends on the library, never the reverse. The library may only gain a NEUTRAL scalar type
(bool / int / float / text / enum-name). The app converts `PropValue` into it at the boundary. If a
proposed design needs the library to know an app type, the design is wrong — stop and re-plan.

OPT-OUT IS REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL
Some builders bind closures or live signals and CANNOT come from static data. These are host-only
by design and must be excluded from the generator, not merely undocumented:
- `on_click` / `on_activate` / `on_change` — behaviour crosses as an `Intent`, never a callback.
- Signal-bound builders, e.g. `DockFrame::rail(..)` (documented as host-only in docs/widgets.md:1704).
- The whole `ScrollBar` widget (view.rs coverage note: host-only, plugins use `Scroll`).
Getting this wrong would let a description claim a capability that silently does nothing — the exact
defect this phase exists to remove.

TYPE MAPPING
Builders take varied argument types: `impl Into<String>`, `f32`, `bool`, `Glyph`, `ButtonVariant`,
`ScrollAxes`, `ToastSeverity`, `LabelSide`. Scalars are direct. Enums arrive as NAMES (consistent
with how glyphs and colours already work in the model) and need a name→value conversion per enum —
generate that too, or the enum list becomes the new drift.

THE DRIFT TEST (the real deliverable)
A test that walks each widget's generated property table and fails when a native builder has no
declarative counterpart and no explicit opt-out marker. Model it on the existing coverage guard
`every_widget_kind_realizes_to_a_live_widget_except_the_host_only_ones`, which already stops a new
`WidgetKind` from silently rendering an empty container (AGENTS.md:775-778).
This test is what would have caught `Input::placeholder` and the scroll axes years ago. It is worth
more than the generator itself — if the generator proves too costly, KEEP THIS and report back
rather than shipping neither.

ACCEPTANCE
- realize.rs holds no property-name string literals for widget-specific settings.
- Adding a builder to a widget without exposing it or marking it host-only FAILS the build.
- Host-only builders are excluded by an explicit marker, and the markers are documented.
- Full workspace green, clippy clean.
- Update view.rs's props-by-kind table + docs/widgets.md.

checklist.title: Design the neutral scalar type + setter trait; confirm heca-grid-ui gains no app types
Build the generator over annotated builder methods
Add explicit host-only opt-out markers (closures, signal-bound builders, ScrollBar)
Generate enum name→value conversion so the enum list is not new drift
Shrink realize_kind to construct-then-feed; remove the per-property string literals
Add the drift test modelled on the existing WidgetKind coverage guard
Update view.rs props table + docs/widgets.md

tasks.title: Expose the two proven-missing widget settings: Input placeholder and Scroll axes
tasks.description:
Closes gaps 2 and 3 of the phase description. These are the two concrete cases that revealed the
whole defect, so they double as the proof that T3's generator works.

SEQUENCING
Do this AFTER T3. Once the generator lands, each of these should reduce to marking the existing
builder plus a test — if either still needs a hand-written arm in realize.rs, T3 is incomplete and
that is the finding to report.
If T3 is dropped or deferred, this task still stands on its own as two hand-written arms.

GAP 2 — Input placeholder
- Native: `Input::placeholder(impl Into<String>)` exists at heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/input.rs:122.
- In use: showcase.rs:264 (the command palette — "Type a command…   (↑/↓ · Ctrl+J/K · Enter)") and
  showcase.rs:698 ("CALLSIGN").
- Declarative: the realize arm (realize.rs:163-176) reads ONLY the value via `text_of(node)`, the
  `name` binding for form submission, and the change intent. No placeholder. A description cannot
  produce an empty input that tells the user what to type.
- Note the naming trap: `Input` uses `text` for the VALUE (view.rs props table: "`Input` | `text`
  (value), `name`"). The placeholder needs its own key; do not overload `text`.

GAP 3 — Scroll axes
- Native: `ScrollRegion::new()` is vertical; `horizontal()`, `both()` and `axes(ScrollAxes)` exist
  at scroll_region.rs:231-247. `ScrollAxes` (scroll_region.rs:101) has `is_vertical`/`is_horizontal`.
- In use and load-bearing: the showcase's ENTIRE root is `ScrollRegion::new().both()`
  (showcase.rs:1897), plus a `.both()` grid demo (showcase.rs:1400-1401).

tasks.title: Expose the clickable Row widget and settle the Row name collision (NEEDS A USER DECISION FIRST)
tasks.description:
Closes gap 4 of the phase description. ⛔ DO NOT START THE CODE — the naming choice is the user's,
and picking it wrong means a renaming churn through the vocabulary, the docs and every example.

THE COLLISION (verified in code 2026-07-25)
Two different things are called Row.
- `heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/row.rs` — a REAL WIDGET. Its own doc header: "a **focusable, clickable
  container** for arbitrary composed content… `Item` is the fixed leading/label/trailing row; `Row`
  is its open cousin: it provides the same interactive chrome — hover tint, active (selected) state
  with an `ActiveMarker`, press flash, focus ring, and `on_activate` (mouse + Enter/Space) — but
  holds **any** children… Use it for rich Dock rows that need to be clicked and selected, where
  `Item`'s slots aren't enough." `on_activate` is at row.rs:96.
- `WidgetKind::Row` — maps to `Flex::row()` (realize.rs:124). A plain horizontal box. No focus, no
  hover, no press, no activation.

CONSEQUENCES
- The interactive Row widget has NO declarative spelling at all. A plugin cannot make a clickable,
  selectable rich row — the exact thing the widget was built for.
- docs/plugin-authoring.md example 2 writes `Row::new().gap(12) … .on_press(intent("plugin.docker.select",
  {"id": …}))` for a clickable table row. That is the WIDGET's behaviour written against the KIND
  that cannot do it. The published example is wrong in a way no reader could detect.
- Anyone reading `WidgetKind::Row` in the app and `Row` in the library reasonably assumes they are
  the same thing. They are not.

THE DECISION TO PUT TO THE USER (do this first, then plan)
Option A — rename the KIND. `WidgetKind::Row` becomes something plainly layout-shaped (`HStack`,
`Hbox`, `Flex`…) and `Row` is freed for the real widget. Truest to the library, but it renames a
kind that already ships in serialized descriptions, the docs and every example — a breaking change
to the model's vocabulary.
Option B — name the new KIND something else and leave `WidgetKind::Row` alone. Cheapest, no
breakage, but the library's `Row` and the model's `Row` stay permanently different things, which is
the confusion that caused this.
Option C — rename the WIDGET in `heca-grid-ui`. Contained inside the library, but it is the widget
that has the better claim to the name.
There is no obviously right answer; it is a judgement about which confusion is cheaper to live with.
Bring the trade-off, do not pick silently. See AGENTS.md: "Discuss architectural changes first."

WORK ONCE DECIDED
- Add a kind for the interactive row and a `realize` arm mapping it to the `Row` widget.
- It is ACTIONABLE, so it needs a `press` event wired to an intent AND a KeyHint target, the same
  way the `Button` arm does (realize.rs:461+ — "wiring its `press` intent to both a click handler
  and a hint target… a click emits it, the picker fires it"). Without the hint target, `prefix+/`
  cannot reach it.
- It also has selected/active state — check against `Item`'s arm for the existing precedent rather
  than inventing a second spelling.
- Apply the rename everywhere it lands: view.rs, realize.rs, docs/widgets.md,
  docs/plugin-authoring.md, README.md, pluggable-chrome-plugin-plan.md.

ACCEPTANCE
- A description can produce a clickable, selectable rich row that behaves exactly like the native one.
- The chosen naming is applied consistently across code AND every document.
- Coverage + `all_lists_every_widget_kind` guards pass.
- USER verifies click, keyboard activation, hover and selected state in the showcase — this is
  interactive behaviour, so tests alone do not close it.

Add the kind + realize arm mapping to the Row widget
Wire press → intent AND a KeyHint target (follow the Button arm), else prefix+/ cannot reach it
Handle selected/active state the way Item's arm already does
Apply the naming decision across view.rs, realize.rs, widgets.md, plugin-authoring.md, README, the plan
Coverage guards pass

tasks.title: Decide the fate of the unused Color value in the model — wire it to theme tokens or remove it
tasks.description:
Closes gap 6, and unblocks the muted-text half of gap 8.

CURRENT STATE — A DECLARED CAPABILITY THAT DOES NOTHING
`PropValue::Color(String)` exists in the model at heca/src/chrome/view.rs:201-202, with the rustdoc
"`#rrggbb` / `#rrggbbaa`, or a theme color token name". Nothing reads it. A grep of realize.rs for
colour handling finds only `glyph_prop` (realize.rs:870) — there is no `color_prop` and no arm that
consumes a `Color` value. It is a promise in the type with no implementation behind it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS
`Label` has no `variant` natively (label.rs — align, color, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough,
font_size, font_scale), and `ViewVariant` is button-shaped (Primary, Secondary, Destructive,
Outline, Ghost, Link — view.rs:169-176, no Muted). So docs/plugin-authoring.md's
`Label::new("Name").variant(Variant::Muted)` has no native equivalent either. Muted text is a
COLOUR. Whether a description can ever produce dimmed secondary text depends entirely on this task.

THE DECISION — put it to the user, do not pick silently
Option A — WIRE IT, TOKEN NAMES ONLY. A description may name a theme token ("muted", "accent",
"danger"); the host resolves it against the active Theme. Raw `#rrggbb` is REJECTED, and the rustdoc
that currently promises hex is corrected. This keeps AGENTS.md's rule ("Is styling a prop? NO";
semantic + colour/glyph NAMES only) — a token name is semantic, a hex literal is not. It also means
themes keep working: a plugin's "muted" follows a theme reload, a hex value would not.
Option B — REMOVE the variant. Smaller model, and no way to express muted text at all. Then
plugin-authoring.md's example must be rewritten, not just corrected.
Recommendation: A, restricted to token names. But it decides how far a plugin may reach into
appearance, so it is the user's call.

WORK IF OPTION A
- Add a reader that resolves a token NAME against the active `Theme`, and reject / ignore anything
  that is not a known token (realize stays TOTAL — unknown name keeps the widget default).
- Correct the `PropValue::Color` rustdoc, which currently advertises hex.
- Decide which kinds accept it. `Label` at minimum (that is the muted-text case). Be conservative:
  every kind that accepts a colour is a kind whose appearance a plugin can influence.
- Verify it survives a runtime theme reload (`prefix+Shift+r`) — that is the whole reason for
  tokens over hex.

WORK IF OPTION B
- Remove the variant, its rustdoc, and any mention in docs/widgets.md and the plan.
- Coordinate with T8: plugin-authoring.md example 2 must lose the muted label, not merely reword.

ACCEPTANCE
- The model no longer declares a capability nothing implements.
- If wired: token names resolve, unknown names keep the default, hex is refused, and a theme reload
  restyles a plugin's text.
- view.rs rustdoc + docs/widgets.md updated either way.
- Colour is visible: the USER looks before it closes.

If A: resolve token names against the Theme; unknown name keeps the default; hex refused
If A: correct the rustdoc that currently promises #rrggbb
If A: decide which kinds accept a colour — be conservative, Label at minimum

tasks.title: OPEN QUESTION (not for this phase): where the builder types must live for a plugin to get editor help
tasks.description:
A recorded question, NOT work to start. Written here so the WASM phase does not rediscover it late.
Expect this to be deferred immediately; it belongs with plugin-08 (the WASM runtime).

THE QUESTION
For a plugin author to get code completion, the builder types must live somewhere their crate can
depend on. Today they cannot.

THE FACTS (verified 2026-07-25)
- The model lives INSIDE THE APP: `ViewNode`, `WidgetKind`, `PropValue`, `Intent` are all in
  heca/src/chrome/view.rs. A plugin is a separate program and cannot depend on the app.
- The workspace has six members and none of them is a plugin kit: heca-core, heca-renderer,
  heca-config, heca-grid-ui, heca, heca-theme (Cargo.toml:2).
- pluggable-chrome-plugin-plan.md never names an SDK crate either — searched, no match for a plugin
  kit crate anywhere in the plan.
- F003/P011/T006's own description says "the WASM SDK re-exports it". With the model inside the app,
  that sentence cannot currently be true of anything.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE FORBIDDEN THING
AGENTS.md:744 rejects `heca-grid-ui` owning `ViewNode`, for two solid reasons: it inverts the crate
graph, and `ViewNode` cannot carry the closures and signals the native chrome depends on. That rule
is about pushing the model DOWN into the widget library. A separate small crate ALONGSIDE — which
both the app and plugins depend on — inverts nothing and is a different question. Do not treat the
settled rule as having already answered it, and do not treat this note as permission either. It is
a question for the user, at the right time.

WHAT ELSE IT TOUCHES
- A plugin written in JavaScript or Python gets no Rust completion regardless. Because the widget
  vocabulary is a CLOSED list with a coverage guard already walking it (`WidgetKind::ALL`), matching
  definitions for other languages could be generated from that same list. Nobody has costed this.
- Whatever T3 generates (the property tables) is the natural source for such generated definitions —
  worth checking that T3's output is reusable rather than private to the app.

WHEN TO PICK THIS UP
With plugin-08 / the WASM runtime, when there is a real plugin to write. Deciding it earlier means
guessing at requirements that do not exist yet.

ACCEPTANCE
None — this task is a placeholder for a decision. Close it by either deferring it to the WASM phase
or, if taken up, replacing it with a real design task after the user has chosen.
